brief: JPMorgan's weekly global note argues the expansion is finding firmer footing even as 2027 financial-stress risk builds. Global consumption (ex-China) grew 2.7%ar through the energy shock; JPM raises its expected slowdown from 1.8%ar to 2%ar this quarter after stronger October US retail sales and Chase card data eased stall risk, aided by falling Brent, jet fuel and gasoline prices. November flash PMI is projected at 53.5, consistent with 1.7%ar DM growth, with GDP revisions showing a profit surge lifting global employment toward 1%ar. The 2027 risk: core inflation persistence and reemerging labor tightening end hopes of disinflation without weak demand, with credit intermediation the pressure point since elevated asset prices depend on capital-market access. The Fed's hawkish shift now exceeds other DM central banks'; JPM expects the December FOMC median dot above 4.5% and now forecasts hikes at the next three meetings. This month's equity fall ties to that shift, and whether it derails business credit is the key growth signal. Regionally: Euro area growth holds near 1.3%ar with two more ECB hikes seen; BoE waits until February; China's growth risk tilts down; BoJ hikes next month then March; EM tightening broadens; Mexico bucks a LatAm slowdown as Brazil contracts.
